> Thanks so much for pointing out this tutorial. I used it to get the table of probabilities of states/ranges at each node following your example. I'm a little confused looking at the resulting table though. The rows are associated with the node number in APE format,

Yes -- and use the function prt() to get those node numbers.  E.g., if your tree is "tr", do prt(tr).

> and the columns are the probabilities of each range, correct?

Yes.  Each column is one of the possible ranges, in this order:

_, A, B, C, AB, AC, BC, ....etc...

(assuming your geog file had "(A B C)" as the order)

> What is the last column where there is no ranges?

There should be no columns that are not ranges. Note that the first "range", "_", represents the null range (living in zero areas...yes this is weird, but removing it is also weird, see discussion on PhyloWiki and Massana et al. on BioArXiv).

> Also, should the "tip nodes" be the same as the geographic character matrix that I input?

I'm not sure what you mean.  The order of species rows in the geography file does not matter, if that's what you're asking.  The tip nodes have (implicit) node numbers in the APE phylo format, the prt() function makes these explicit.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Ah, I see.  That's just an issue with the APE plot function.  There actually is an option I put into plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() at some point to deal with this. It is "xlims:

xlims
# Same as in plot.phylo x.lim. Default is basically c(0,treeheight), so
#' if tiplabels are getting cut off, try e.g. xlims=c(0,1.5*treeheight)

So, if your tree is 83 million years old at the root, add this option to the plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() command:

xlims=c(0,1.5*83)

Adjust "1.5" as needed, until it looks right.

Additional helpful options of plot_BioGeoBEARS_results() -- make sure to do
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")

...to enable.

=====================
* tiplabel_adj Justification for tiplabel boxes (same as "adj" parameter of text() ). Default is c(0.5). Left justification: c(0). Right: c(1). Justification top left: c(0,0), etc.

* You can also change "tipcex" (tip character expansion)
tipcex cex value for the tiplabels (scaling factor, i.e. 0.5 is half size)

* show.tip.label Same as for APE's \code{plot.phylo}.

* xlims Same as in plot.phylo x.lim. Default is basically c(0,treeheight), so
if tiplabels are getting cut off, try e.g. xlims=c(0,1.5*treeheight).

* ylims Same as in plot.phylo y.lim. Default is basically c(0,numtips), so
if the spacing between the title and time axis and the tree are too big,
try e.g. ylims=c(0+10,numtips-10). Trial and error will get you there.

See: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-phylo/2013-March/002540.html
=====================

Another option is show.tip.label=FALSE, then use the text() command to plot tip labels yourself.  Yet another option is manual editing/fixing of the tip labels etc. in Adobe Illustrator or in Inkscape (which is similar but free).

Cheers,
Nick

Thanks!

Robin

On Sat, Oct 28, 2017 at 3:52 AM, XXX wrote:
> Hi Nick,
>
> I am having some issues trying to get a BioGeoBEARS analysis to run and was wondering if you could give me some feedback. Basically, I am getting an error message saying that some tip ranges are not allowed according to the states_list. I have tried using a custom states_list which defines all allowed ranges, but that does not seem to solve the problem either.

An area_adjacency matrix will limit the state space -- meaning, limit the list of allowed ranges.  Another thing that will limit the list of allowed states/ranges is the max_range_size setting, if max_range_size=4, then any ranges with more than 4 areas are disallowed. If you then had a tip in the tipranges/geography file with 5 areas, you would get that area.

I suspect your problem is something simple, like having uncommented the area_adjacency line, but then forgetting to re-comment-it-out when you use a different strategy like the custom ranges list.

You probably saw this, but it gives some advice -- I would recommend the custom modification of the ranges list, then you know exactly what you are doing:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#areas_adjacency_matrix2

>
> Here is an example of what happens: I am working on a global scale and have defined an area adjacency matrix of the major terrestrial zoogeographic realms. I have allowed for a connection between the Palearctic and Nearctic (via Beringia), but the Sino-Japanese region is only adjacent to the Palearctic. However, it is of course perfectly conceivable (I think) to potentially have a range that includes all three areas, but that does not seem to be allowed according to my adjacency matrix.
>
> Maybe I am missing something blatantly obvious, but I can't seem to figure this out (even when specifying my custom states_list). Any suggestions on how to fix this?

You should be able to do the custom states list, then look at your states_list or ranges_list and see whether or not e.g. Palearctic+Neartic+Sino-Japan is in that list -- that's the key thing.

Cheers!
Nick
